title: Retire the scheduler-authority-lease absence entry and drive the real fencing surface
description:
Objective: retire the one absence-manifest entry whose behaviour has landed, so repo-root `pnpm test` returns to exit 0. Created by architect-0b81de40 2026-08-09 to resolve a cross-task deadlock: this single red is blocking THREE finished tasks and nobody owned the file.

WHY THIS EXISTS. `packages/testkit/src/foundation/foundation-fault-schedule.ts` declares `schedule:j4-stale-lease-enforcement` as `productionBehaviorAbsent("exported lease/authority fencing surface", "probe:scheduler-authority-lease")`. That was honest until task-8ee125d0 (commit 239aa4f) published the scheduler root surface. The probe measures the PUBLIC EXPORT SURFACE, so it now resolves and returns PASS_EXPECTED while the manifest still declares ABSENT, and the ratchet fires exactly as designed. The file's own doc comment at lines 56-61 predicted this verbatim: "Adding the re-export is what flips it: the probe goes red against the declared outcome and forces the manifest entry to be updated to PASS_EXPECTED." This task is that update. The ratchet is working correctly - do not disable it, weaken it, or make the probe lie.

MEASURED 2026-08-09: `npx vitest run --root . tests/fault/foundation/j4-replan-stale.test.ts` -> 1 failed / 14 passed, the sole failure being `schedule:j4-stale-lease-enforcement` expecting PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT and receiving PASS_EXPECTED. Repo-root `pnpm test` is otherwise green (2866 passing at last measurement). The sibling blocker on `packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts` is ALREADY FIXED - that suite passes 14/14 - so this is the last one.

NOT A ONE-LINE EDIT, and this is the part to get right. Flipping the declared outcome to PASS is not sufficient and would be dishonest on its own: the row's claim is "a command carrying a superseded lease epoch must be refused by the authority surface", and its executor at `tests/fault/foundation/j4-replan-stale.test.ts:187` is still `(entry) => produceAbsenceOutcome(entry)`, which only probes the export surface and asserts nothing about behaviour. A real executor must replace it, following the pattern every other PASS row in that file already uses: exercise the production surface, assert the specific refusal code, then `return passExpected()`. Per the lease-presence handoff the relevant code is the stale-epoch refusal from `fenceAuthority`, now reachable from the `@moe/scheduler` root.

Deliverable: the manifest entry flipped to PASS, a real behaviour-driving executor for that row, and the now-historical doc comment corrected. Repo-root `pnpm test` back to exit 0.

NOT in scope: changing `fenceAuthority` or anything under `packages/scheduler/src/authority/**`; touching any other manifest entry or probe; retiring `probe:scheduler-authority-lease` itself if any other row still references it; relaxing the ratchet mechanism or the `foundation-spec.test.ts` guards that police the manifest.

Hard dependencies: none. task-8ee125d0's commit 239aa4f is already in HEAD and is what triggered this.

Owned paths: packages/testkit/src/foundation/foundation-fault-schedule.ts and tests/fault/foundation/j4-replan-stale.test.ts.
Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/testkit typecheck && npx vitest run --root . tests/fault/foundation/j4-replan-stale.test.ts && pnpm test
definitionOfDone: The `schedule:j4-stale-lease-enforcement` row in foundation-fault-schedule.ts declares PASS instead of productionBehaviorAbsent, and no other manifest row or probe definition is changed.

Its executor in j4-replan-stale.test.ts drives the REAL production surface — it obtains fenceAuthority (or the equivalent published entry point) from the @moe/scheduler package root, submits a command carrying a superseded lease epoch, and asserts the specific stable refusal code AND the refusing layer, before returning passExpected(). It must no longer call produceAbsenceOutcome.

The executor is proven load-bearing by mutation: neutralise the epoch comparison in the assertion (never delete a line) and confirm this row goes red naming that code, then restore and verify the restore against `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` rather than `git status`.
The doc comment at foundation-fault-schedule.ts:56-61, which describes this probe as the live ABSENT example, is corrected so it no longer states as current a condition that has been retired.
Repo-root `pnpm test` exits 0, and `pnpm --filter @moe/testkit typecheck` exits 0, with fresh captured output quoted as evidence.
Only the two owned paths are staged and committed, verified with `git show --stat`.
taskRails: The ratchet is working correctly. Do NOT disable it, skip the row, loosen the foundation-spec.test.ts guards that police the manifest, or make a probe report something it did not measure. The only honest fix is to make the declared outcome true and prove it.

PASS must mean the behaviour was exercised, not that the export exists. An executor that flips to passExpected() without asserting a real refusal is exactly the fabricated pass epic rail 4 forbids, and would convert a working ratchet into a permanent lie.
Assert the reason code AND the refusing layer, never merely that the command was refused. A second refusal layer answering first would leave this green while no longer testing the authority surface.

Do not edit packages/scheduler/src/authority/** or any other package to make this pass. If the surface genuinely cannot be driven from the package root, report_blocked rather than reaching into a foreign path.

Mutation drills run in a SHARED worktree where another agent's completion hook can commit your edit; git status will then report clean because HEAD holds the mutation. Capture `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` before mutating, verify the restore against that sha, keep the mutated window to one test run, and re-run the full gate afterwards.
Commit by explicit pathspec only — never a bare git commit, never git add -A. Several agents share this working directory.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) FLIP-ONLY WAS REJECTED. The tempting fix is one character: change `productionBehaviorAbsent(...)` to `PASS` and the suite goes green. That would be a fabricated pass. The row's claim is behavioural — 'a command carrying a superseded lease epoch must be refused by the authority surface' — but its executor is `produceAbsenceOutcome`, which only measures whether the export exists. Flipping the declaration without replacing the executor would leave a row that asserts a behaviour nobody tested, permanently, and convert a correctly-working ratchet into a lie. So the executor is replaced FIRST and the declaration flipped second.
(2) ORDER MATTERS AND IS DELIBERATE. Write the real executor before flipping the manifest. With the executor real and the declaration still ABSENT, the row fails for a NEW and informative reason (it now returns passExpected from real behaviour, versus a declared ABSENT), which proves the executor actually ran. Flipping first would make the suite green immediately and you would never learn whether the executor works.
(3) DRIVE IT FROM THE PACKAGE ROOT, not a deep import. `fenceAuthority`, `parseLeaseRecord`, `parseProof` and `parseClock` are all exported from `packages/scheduler/src/index.ts` as of commit 239aa4f — that publication is precisely what fired this ratchet. Importing from the root is also what `packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts` enforces; a deep import would trip that separate suite.
(4) SCOPE HELD DELIBERATELY TIGHT: two files, one manifest row, one executor, one stale doc comment. Every other manifest row and every probe definition is left alone.

MEASURED 2026-08-09, not taken from a report:
- **The failure**: `npx vitest run --root . tests/fault/foundation/j4-replan-stale.test.ts` -> 1 failed / 14 passed. Diff is exactly `- PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT / + PASS_EXPECTED` at `j4-replan-stale.test.ts:201`.

The other rows in that array use the bare `PASS` constant.
- **The executor** is `tests/fault/foundation/j4-replan-stale.test.ts:187`: `"schedule:j4-stale-lease-enforcement": (entry) => produceAbsenceOutcome(entry),`. Every real row in that file follows a different, consistent pattern: build a hostile input, `expect(...)` the exact refusal shape, then `return passExpected()`. Copy that pattern — examples at lines ~90-130 (`j4-finding-without-evidence-refused`, `j4-round-limit-requires-explicit-escalation`, `j4-stale-envelope-version-rejected`).
- **The production surface, confirmed exported from the @moe/scheduler ROOT** (`packages/scheduler/src/index.ts:62-65`): `fenceAuthority`, `parseClock`, `parseLeaseRecord`, `parseProof`.
- **Signature** (`packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-fencing.ts:97`): `fenceAuthority(record: unknown, authority: unknown, commandKind: string, legalStates: readonly LeaseState[]): Fenced`. It parses the record and the proof first and returns a malformed rejection when either fails — which is the nearer refusal layer this test must NOT accidentally hit.

That handoff also records that token redaction is scoped to REJECTIONS while epochs are retained, which is what makes an epoch assertion possible at all.
- **The sibling blocker is already gone**: `packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts` passes 14/14 as of this measurement. The doc comment at `effect-test-fixtures.ts:15-20` now explains the prose-matching hazard instead of tripping it. Do not re-fix it.
planningNotes.risks:
1. **The nearer refusal layer is the trap.** `fenceAuthority` parses the record and proof BEFORE it compares epochs, so a fixture that is slightly malformed returns `AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT` and the test passes for entirely the wrong reason while looking correct. Assert the specific stale-epoch code AND the refusing layer, and sanity-check that the same fixture with a CURRENT epoch is ACCEPTED — without that positive control the test could pass by refusing everything.
2. **`PASS` must mean exercised, not exported.** This is the whole point of the task; an executor returning `passExpected()` without a real `expect` on a refusal is the fabricated pass epic rail 4 forbids.
3. **MUTATION DRILL IN A SHARED WORKTREE** (`mem:mutation-drills-in-shared-worktree`): another agent's completion hook commits the WHOLE tree, so your in-place mutation can be swept into someone else's commit. After that, `git checkout -- <path>` restores the MUTATED blob and `git status` reports clean, because HEAD now holds the mutation — the only signal is a failing test. Capture `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` BEFORE mutating, verify the restore against that sha rather than against `git status`, keep the mutated window to a single test run, and re-run the full gate after the last drill.
4. **Do not touch any other manifest row or probe.** `foundation-spec.test.ts` polices the manifest (it asserts every PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT entry has a resolvable probe, among others); changing a neighbouring row can redden guards that have nothing to do with this fix.
5. **Do not retire `probe:scheduler-authority-lease` itself** without checking whether another row still references it — grep first. Removing a probe another entry depends on would break a different guard.
6. **Do not edit `packages/scheduler/src/authority/**` or any other package** to make this pass (task rail 4). If the surface cannot be driven from the package root, report_blocked.
7. **Import from `@moe/scheduler` root, never a deep path** — `package-boundary.test.ts` scans source contents for internal scheduler paths and a deep import (or even a path-quoting comment) trips it.
8. Root `pnpm test` is the real gate here and it is shared: if it is red for some OTHER reason when you run it, attribute by path and name the file rather than assuming it is yours.
